abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions that matter for the app's real variation (cards, move tables, label maps) stretch well, but the card-list pipeline is copy-pasted and would be duplicated again for any new resource page, and a couple of rules are magic numbers rather than named constants.

findings.issue: The 'pokemon refs → deduped, dex-sorted CardData[]' pipeline (idFromUrl, id>10000 filter, seen-set, speciesCard, sort) is copy-pasted three times (moves :627-636, abilities :675-684, types :745-755), so a new resource page copies it a fourth time and rule changes are made in triplicate.
findings.suggestion: Extract a helper like cardsFromPokemonRefs(refs: NamedRef[]): Promise<CardData[]> next to speciesCard, and let the three page loaders call it.

findings.issue: Sprite resolution is duplicated: speciesCard defaults to mediaSprite(species.id) (:220) while getHomeData builds its own front_default ?? mediaSprite(id) fallback, so a 'default Pokémon has a different name' bug (Deoxys-class) must be fixed in two places and they can drift.
findings.suggestion: Make speciesCard the only place that resolves a sprite (pass the default Pokémon record in, or add a speciesSprite(species) helper) and have getHomeData call it.

findings.issue: The `${name} – Pokédex` / `Not found – Pokédex` title ternary is repeated in five route files; changing the title format means editing all of them.
findings.suggestion: Add a pageTitle(name | null) helper (e.g. in lib/format.ts) or share it via a small head helper the routes call.

findings.issue: Not-found is handled by a {notFound: true} DTO union plus a per-route branch and head ternary in four routes, instead of TanStack Router's notFound()/notFoundComponent; the loader also succeeds with a 200 rather than a 404 status (which the spec encourages).
findings.suggestion: Throw notFound() from the loader (or wrap getNotFound) and define a router-level notFoundComponent, removing the branch and head ternary from every route.

findings.issue: The alternate-forms cutoff is a magic id > 10000 repeated at :288 (home, as id <= 10000), :630, :678 and :749, unlike EXCLUDED_TYPES which is a named constant at :6.
findings.suggestion: Hoist a MAX_SPECIES_ID / isAlternateForm(id) constant next to EXCLUDED_TYPES and use it everywhere.

findings.issue: All six server functions use identity validators like .validator((data: HomeFilters) => data), which buys type inference but validates nothing about client-controlled GET inputs (e.g. a bogus type name is only caught later by the options check in getHomeData).
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as a typing idiom, but a real schema (or at least trimming/clamping in one place) would make the server boundary self-documenting.

findings.issue: Shared view DTOs (CardData, MoveRow, EvolutionNode) are exported from data.server.ts and imported type-only by client components; this is allowed by import protection, but the docs recommend splitting client-safe types into a shared module so the seam stays obvious.
findings.suggestion: Move CardData/MoveTableData/EvolutionNode (and the HomeFilters-like input shapes) into lib/types.ts and keep data.server.ts for runtime logic.

findings.issue: The 'strip empty/default search params' logic is written twice inside the same component (update():50-58 and linkSearch():76-81), so a new filter or a change to the omit-defaults rule must be made in both.
findings.suggestion: Extract a buildSearch(filters: HomeFilters) helper used by both update() and the pagination links.

summary: This is a clean, current TanStack Start app: file-based routes, server functions behind a .server.ts module that import protection keeps out of the client, URL-driven filter state, and shared card/table components that give the app real seams. The editability ceiling is set by one 778-line data module that copy-pastes its card-list pipeline three times, duplicates sprite resolution, and by per-route repetition of the title and not-found patterns. Extending to a new resource section or changing the API/cache policy is straightforward; removing a feature or fixing a cross-list bug takes a handful of well-aimed edits instead of one.
